PART 1 (0–147 s)
Emotion 2 · Sound off 2 · Pacing 2 · Composition 3
- 6 s: The narration says "Nina rents, with $92,000 saved," but the picture is an abstract chart. Nina doesn't appear anywhere in Part 1. Fix: open on Nina at her rental door with a $92,000 stack at her feet, then pull back to the street.
- 18 s: The caption still reads "with cash: 3 in 4" while the voice has moved on to stocks (half). At 92 s the stocks bar is short under "first house: lit" while the voice says $485,063 behind. Fix: change each caption and bar on the spoken word, not one line later.
- 79 s: The $48,410 cash result has no number and no light on the house. The shot is a close-up of a cash brick. Fix: light the first house's window as "$48,410 ahead" is spoken, then turn it off at 92 s as the stocks pile shoots up.
- 116–128 s: The stocks pile drops back to tiny with no explanation, and "$92,000 + a deposit every month" shows up about 10 s late. Fix: keep the tall pile and break it into one base brick plus many thin monthly slices dropping in as the voice describes them.

PART 2 (147–388 s)
Emotion 3 · Sound off 3 · Pacing 2 · Composition 2
- 157 s: The "rent tag, 5 percent" line plays over an empty dark street. The tag isn't seen until 453 s. Fix: close in on the tag on Nina's door here, so the payoff later has something to call back to.
- 197 s: "The darkest house is the very first one" is said, but nothing marks house #1. Fix: dim the January 1991 house to black and drop a spotlight on it.
- 257 s: "The dark house got darker" is told by text only. The stacks are small and cut off by the lower-third caption. Fix: frame the June 2006 house large and actually fade its windows as the stocks figure appears. Lift the stacks above the safe area.
- 337–378 s: Three stacked captions cover the grid. The bar chart's title is clipped ("uyer ahead… sta"). The 15-year grid is still 307 cells and looks about as lit as the 10-year one. Fix: one caption at a time, kept off the grid. Shrink the grid to 247 cells and make roughly 4 in 5 of them visibly dark.

PART 3 (388–480 s)
Emotion 2 · Sound off 3 · Pacing 2 · Composition 2
- 391–399 s: About 16 s of an empty frame: a bare axis, with the street jammed into the top-right corner. Fix: run the two growth lines (stocks over homes), then cut to the half-lit street on "yet."
- 422 s: The camera drifts. The $400k stack is cut off at the left edge and the monthly gap is never shown. Fix: lock the two-stack shot and add monthly slices to the pile while the house stack grows.
- 461 s: The text says "flip point 5.1%" while the tag reads 4.83%, and the street doesn't react. This is the episode's key idea and it never gets a picture. Fix: put the tag and the street in the same frame and have houses flip as the tag sweeps from 4.8 to 5.4.
- 477 s: "stability, control" plays over the rental building. Fix: show Nina at an owned house's door. Remove "family," since it isn't in the narration.

PART 4 (480–524 s)
Emotion 2 · Sound off 3 · Pacing 2 · Composition 3
- 482–489 s: The limits card is 7 lines of small text, including credits that aren't narrated. Fix: show only the four narrated limits, larger. Move the credits to the end card.
- 493 s: An empty "Nina's question" box, then a slide of text recaps the whole result. Fix: replay it on the street itself, lit three ways (cash / stocks / 15 years).
- 511 s: The text "Nina's own month: not on this street" is a line from 186 s. The voice is asking how long she'll stay. Fix: show Nina at the end of the street looking toward unlit plots ahead of her.
- 515–522 s: The "coin flip, the rent tag tips it" ending sits on about 10 s of a static building, with the tag unreadable. Fix: close in on the tag, nudge it, and let the street behind flip about half. End on Nina.

Across all four parts: the source line, the "ILLUSTRATIVE" badge and the disclaimer appear in every frame and take attention away from the data. Show them once per part, smaller.
